unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cut two things the first draft kept. The first is the claim that Seward himself was 'too simple a nature to know' which was mask and which nature. The second is the list 'never petty or personal; his talk was large'. As a result, 'What was more unusual' now compares only to 'the youth of his sympathies'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The mask-versus-features sentence and 'Henry Adams thought it charming' survive.

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision dropped 'The inevitable followed, as a child fresh from the nursery should have had the instinct to foresee...'. It also dropped 'Going over the experience again, long after all the great actors were dead, he struggled to see where he had blundered.' As a result, the paragraph explaining his obedience now begins abruptly after 'there it ended'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'Many a shock was Henry Adams to meet in the course of a long life' still signals retrospection.

evidence.quote: The inevitable followed, as a child fresh from the nursery should have had the instinct to foresee, but the young man on the edge of life never dreamed.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'Going over the experience again...' sentence at the head of revision paragraph 22. Optionally also restore 'The inevitable followed...' before the Virginia paragraph.

unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The old narrator's backward look and the ironic foreshadowing of the young man's naivety disappear. The rupture reads as plain chronology instead of a lesson the narrator is still reconsidering.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Retrospective frame around the Sumner rupture removed

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision removed the closing judgment that 'no man living needed so much education as the new President but that all the education he could get would not be enough'. It also removed 'Of course he looked anxiously for a sign of character'. The portrait now ends at 'lack of apparent force'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The 'would have lost' frame and verbatim V6 survive, so the misjudgment is still flagged.

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cut the 'He justly thought...' sentence, which the first draft kept in compressed form. As a result, 'qualities that warranted dogmatism' names no qualities. The later 'supremely fitted by knowledge and experience' also loses its setup, including 'his knowledge of the world', which contrasts with Southern ignorance.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Sumner is still 'the boy's oldest friend', who 'stood quite alone'.
